field_guide.cik: Company identifier stored as text. Join filings using both CIK and accession number.
field_guide.fact_name: Raw XBRL concept. Related concepts may have different definitions.
field_guide.fact_category: Taxonomy namespace. Compare concepts only under compatible definitions.
field_guide.fact_value: Value in the returned unit. NULL is missing and never implies zero.
field_guide.unit: Original units. USD values are unscaled dollars.
field_guide.end_date: Fact period end. It can precede the filing's fiscal year.
field_guide.fiscal_year: Fiscal-year label of the disclosure. Verify the fact's actual end_date.
field_guide.fiscal_period: Source fiscal-period label. Check period length and frame for flows.
field_guide.frame: Supplementary period indicator. A missing frame does not establish annual duration.
field_guide.filed_date: Submission date, distinct from the fact period end.
field_guide.form_type: Source filing form. One period may be disclosed in several filings.
field_guide.accession_number: SEC submission identifier. A matching filings row may be absent.
field_guide.dimension_segment: Segment scope if supplied. Absence alone does not prove comparability.
field_guide.dimension_geography: Geographic scope if supplied. Absence alone does not prove comparability.

interpretation_notes: Check end_date, fiscal_period, frame and form_type before comparing flows across periods.
Check concept, unit, period length and dimensions before identifying repeats.
Repeated disclosures can reflect revisions. Retain fact IDs and accession numbers and do not sum repeats.
Do not conflate net income, parent-attributable income, operating income and pretax income.

Personnel-related costs and allocated overhead costs also increased $45.3 million for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2025, compared to the prior fiscal year, as a result of increased headcount and overall costs to support the growth in our business, and increased stock-based compensation primarily related to additional equity awards granted to existing and new employees. Additionally, amortization of capitalized internal-use software development costs and acquired developed technology intangible assets also increased $37.5 million and $11.1 million, respectively, for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2025, compared to the prior fiscal year. The remaining increase in cost of product revenue was primarily attributable to $7.7 million in costs incurred by us during fiscal 2025 in connection with a restructuring plan for a majority-owned subsidiary.

I've reached the tool budget. I have enough evidence for a supported answer on the main operational changes, acquisitions, and restructuring actions in FY2025 (year ended January 31, 2025), with one limitation on the restructuring note details.

**Snowflake Inc. — notable operational changes, acquisitions and restructuring during fiscal 2025 (year ended January 31, 2025)**

**Acquisitions (business combinations)**
- **Datavolo, Inc.** — acquired all outstanding capital stock on **November 25, 2024**. Datavolo was a privately held company that built dataflow infrastructure for creating, managing and observing multimodal data pipelines for enterprise AI; acquired for its developed technology and talent. Preliminary purchase consideration fair value was **$106.8 million**, comprising **0.5 million shares of common stock valued at $87.7 million** and **$19.1 million in cash**. Snowflake also issued **0.4 million shares** to certain Datavolo employees (fair value **$64.6 million**) subject to four-year vesting, accounted for as post-combination stock-based compensation. (10-K FY2025, Item 7 chunk 1640147/snow-20250131:252583; Item 8 chunk 1640147/snow-20250131:423815 and :424235)
- **Other fiscal 2025 business combinations** — the filing refers to "other fiscal 2025 business combinations" whose revenue and net loss were not material, and states pro forma information for them was not presented as effects were immaterial (chunks 1640147/snow-20250131:428380 and :430283). The risk-factor discussion lists **Night Shift Development, Inc.** (a privately held data analytics firm focused on the U.S. public sector) among companies acquired since the beginning of fiscal 2024 (chunk 1640147/snow-20250131:132790). The filing does not, in the excerpts retrieved, give a separate purchase price for Night Shift or name every "other" fiscal 2025 target.
- For context, the FY2024-period acquisitions (Neeva, LeapYear, Mountain/Mobilize.Net, Samooha) are described as prior-year transactions, not fiscal 2025 events (chunks :435143, :439027, :437118, :430506).

**Restructuring**
- Snowflake incurred costs under a **restructuring plan for a majority-owned subsidiary** during fiscal 2025: **$7.7 million** recorded in cost of product revenue and **$11.0 million** in research and development (chunks 1640147/snow-20250131:294342 and :299887). The retrieved excerpts do not give the plan's approval date, headcount affected, or total expected charges; a dedicated restructuring note was not retrieved within the tool budget, so the full scope of the plan cannot be confirmed from the evidence gathered.

**Leadership/operational changes**
- **February 2024:** Frank Slootman retired as CEO and **Sridhar Ramaswamy** was appointed CEO.
- **July 2024:** Grzegorz Czajkowski (former EVP, Engineering and Support) resigned; **September 2024:** Vivek Raghunathan appointed SVP, Engineering and Support.
- **February 2025:** CFO Michael P. Scarpelli notified of intention to retire once a successor is appointed (to move into an advisory role).
- **March 2025:** CRO Christopher W. Degnan notified of intention to retire; **Michael Gannon** appointed to replace him.
(10-K FY2025, Item 1A chunk 1640147/snow-20250131:116888)

**Other items noted**
- Shares issued in the December 2023 Samooha combination that had been treated as treasury stock were transferred to the Company and **retired during fiscal 2025** (chunk 1640147/snow-20250131:340520).
- FY2024 included a **$7.1 million impairment** of capitalized internal-use software no longer probable of completion; FY2025 and FY2023 impairments were not material (chunk 1640147/snow-20250131:423197).

**Uncertainty:** The exact number and identity of all "other fiscal 2025 business combinations" and the detailed terms of the majority-owned-subsidiary restructuring plan (approval date, headcount, total charge) were not fully retrieved; the figures above are the directly disclosed amounts in the FY2025 Form 10-K excerpts cited.
